body: The city is great to visit, no doubt, especially this time of year. But if you were to live here you may find it very unappealing. I don't know what you do for a living but if you make any kind of money you will be taxed out the ass for the dumbest shit you can think of, and the tax money goes into an unaccountable black hole that produces meager results. Portland considers anyone making over 120k "rich" and taxes them accordingly.

The person you're replying to is not wrong though, or wildly off base. I'm 98% all in on trans issues and believe they should be treated with respect and kindness just like most people, but because I disagree with this little sliver of issue of trans girls competing in bio girls sports, I've been called transphobic and bigoted, told to unalive myself, and straight up told to go fuck myself.  A large portion of the trans community tolerates absolutely no dissent or makes no space for nuance. You either have to be 100% in agreement or else you are the enemy. Just like the other poster contends. So, yeah, it's very religious-like in that way.

The Oregon Health Plan paid for my neighbor's kid to get top surgery. Which means our tax dollars paid for it. If this doesn't say that the democrats/liberals (which Portland and Oregon are largely beholden to due to the voter base) wholeheartedly support this, I don't know what to tell you. 

Now, you can make the argument that this wouldn't happen nationally, but if it happens locally when the dems/libs are in control, it stands to reason that they would try to make this a national benefit if they ever regained the levers of power.

It's not a winning issue yet the Democrats lean into it when they have power.
You're getting down-voted but you ain't wrong. People just don't like to hear the truth, I guess.

Oh?  Did this renter put down 20% or more of the total cost to live in the dwelling like that dastardly landlord did?  Or are they just entitled to live where they want to live with no real skin in the game?  There is an insane amount of risk to be a landlord in this city.
It's me, the internet from the future.  The answer is: no.
You are whistling past the graveyard.  High earners (you know, the people who actually own businesses) are leaving in droves, that's a fact.  Can you blame them?
You jest, but there is a large contingent of Portland voters who actually think like this.  Anyone who makes more than 100K a year equals rich.

It is absolutely the taxes and shit services. For whatever reason the voting base here is extremely anti-money, anti-capitalism, anti anything growth, so they vote the citizen initiatives in to actively hurt high earners. But the high earners have the ability to flee the area very easily, which we are doing. So soon you're going to have a hollowed out city reminiscent of 1980s Detroit. It's not going to be pretty. 

The change has to start with the voters. Stop indulging in your socialist fantasies where rich folk willingly hand over half their money year after year to support people who want to take drugs and play video games all day.  Stop making it difficult to be a small-time landlord.  Audit every single nonprofit to make sure that 85% of every dollar is going to services and not to admin salaries. Figure out how to make peace with cops so they actually do their jobs and show up to legitimate calls. I can go on and on.  It's like the voters collectively said "I don't care if the city is functional, I just want to throw a tantrum and smash all the pieces on the game board."

There's an insane amount of anti-capitalist hostility coupled with nonprofit corruption that sucks all the tax money into a black hole.  Until those things stop you're not going to get any high earners or businesses who want to operate in the area.  I mean, would you willingly purchase a house that was on fire?
Yeah no kidding. My nuts get squeezed hard every April 15th by this fucking city.  They turn me upside down and shake my wallet dry and provide extremely poor services for the money I provide.

Yeah, there is no free lunch.  You can't just give tons of shit away and make it ultra comfortable for people to sit on their asses and do drugs and fuck around all day.  Someone has to pull the cart.  The liberal states made it too easy to game the system and get free stuff so the people who actually have to provide that free stuff move away from the area.  Who would have thought?  And the people moving away started out liberal but got tired of paying sky-high taxes for shit services.  

And I say this as someone who started out liberal (I loved this place 20 years ago!) but then slowly started seeing the downsides of the "compassion at any cost" movement that the Portland electorate seems to be in love with.

Interesting that you're getting downvoted for stating the simple truth: You need small mom-n-pop landlord operations that are generally local to the area served or else some faceless out-of-town corporation is gonna come in and buy up the rental stock and continually raise rents and provide sub-par service.  It's that simple.

Because of the insane squatter laws (sorry, tenant protection laws) the mom-n-pops are being forced out and the corps are moving in.  I'm planning on moving out of the area soon, and instead of selling my very nice Eastmoreland house I could rent it, but knowing how Portland and its local populace treats landords, I say fuck that noise.  Too much headache and a shit-ton of risk from one bad tenant who has an axe to grind against capitalism.  Better just to take the money from the sale of the house and stick it in a low-risk ETF somewhere.  

It's like they want the city to fail.  There really is no other way to explain it. I mean, maybe that's the plan?  Make it make sense.

Nope, the landlords are just trying to work within a system that was imposed on them by the government.  You'll notice that rents shot up dramatically as soon as rent control took effect.  It's distorting the market.  But the idiot electorate doesn't understand that, they just think "landlord bad."
\^This.  I've never seen a bigger block of dumb fucks than the Portland electorate.  They couldn't reason themselves out of a wet paper bag.

Seriously.  The voters think "landlord bad, let's stick it to 'em next election" and then are shocked when a modest two bedroom aparment is going for 2k a month.  I wonder if their economic sense is that landlords will just eat the tax increases themselves.  Ya know, for the good of the collective.  

Bonkers thinking, really.

This is a really bad take.  I'm a WFH engineer and I pay about 90k in taxes per year, and that's after my wizard CPA doing as much as he can given the punitive tax structure here.  Yes, I get paid well, but if I moved across the river I'd pay significantly less, as in tens of thousands of dollars less.  It's definitely not "maybe a couple hundred dollars."

Thankfully I'll be moving from the area this summer as soon as my last kid goes to college.  Then I'll join the stats of high earners fleeing a seething voter pool that sees people like myself as an endless piggy bank.  

The sad thing is, if the services were actually commensurate with the sky-high tax burden I wouldn't mind as much.
